THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 2 times, as “WALKER G H”, “WALKER GEORGE H”, 1836-06-22: 2 lots in the platted town — lot 1 of block 37 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L1BL37CHIOT, as printed); lot 6 of block 37 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L6BL37CHIOT, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $9650.00 (ls1526, ls1527). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $9650.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: WALKER G H matches George H Walker: the forename names George H Walker of the 4 people of this surname, and the forename agrees as an initial only. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

merge_ruling.for_merge: Both are Georges in chicago_democrat_1833_1835 and the town holds no third Walker of that forename. Kept verbatim from T-0839 so the argument survives its refusal.
merge_ruling.against_merge: EACH MIDDLE INITIAL IS PRINTED TWICE, BY INDEPENDENT HANDS. George E. Walker is 'George E. Walker' in the Democrat's letter list of 2 July 1834 and 'Walker, George E.' in Fergus's old-settler death notice of 9 November 1874. George H. Walker is 'WALKER, GEORGE H' on the 1832 Black Hawk enrollment roll and 'G. H. Walker' in the Democrat's letter list of 1 April 1834. A copyist's mis-set is the WHOLE ground for folding a contradicted middle initial, and it does not survive two independent attestations on each side: four printings, two sources apiece, E twice and H twice. The town's other Walker cards are James and Jeremiah. T-0480's research adds, without asserting it, a George E. Walker in an 1835 Illinois land record near Utica — competing geography, recorded and not leaned on.
